record.paper_title: Achievement sets – current results and open problems
record.original_question: Can every infinite achievable set be written as the algebraic sum of two achievable sets of Hausdorff dimension 0?

evidence.quote: Can every infinite achievable set be decomposed into the sum of two achievable sets of Hausdorff dimension 0?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(x_n)_{n=1}^{\infty}$ be a sequence of real numbers with $x_n \to 0$ and $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} |x_n| < \infty$. The achievement set (set of subsums) of $(x_n)$ is defined by
$$A(x_n) = \Big\{ \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \varepsilon_n x_n : (\varepsilon_n) \in \{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}} \Big\} \subseteq \mathbb{R}.$$
A subset $E \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is called an achievable set if $E = A(x_n)$ for some such sequence $(x_n)$. For sets $B, C \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, their algebraic (Minkowski) sum is $B + C = \{b + c : b \in B,\, c \in C\}$. The Hausdorff dimension of a set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ is denoted $\dim_H(S)$.

Question: Is it true that every infinite achievable set $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ can be written as
$$A = B + C,$$
where $B$ and $C$ are achievable sets with $\dim_H(B) = \dim_H(C) = 0$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem in a recent survey on achievement sets (2025). Web searches did not surface any published resolution; related work studies Hausdorff dimensions of achievement sets but does not appear to settle this decomposition question.

status_evidence.snippet: Studies achievement sets and their Hausdorff dimensions but does not address the decomposition question.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on Hausdorff dimension of achievement sets exists, but no resolution of the decomposition question is found.

status_evidence.title: Signed null sequences and Hausdorff dimension
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on Hausdorff dimension in the context of subsum sets.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature continues to study dimensions of subsum/achievement sets without resolving this problem.
